description:
## Problem

`run_osd_campaign` drives its per-block evaluator through a sequential `FnMut(OsdBlockContext<'_>) -> OsdBlockOutcome` loop, so `ebch_osd_awgn_campaign` runs one thread (observed: `Threads: 1`, 99.7% of one core on a 24-thread host during the 2026-08-27 rigorous campaign). The crate ships rayon and a parallel executor stack that the other campaign binaries (`dvb_t2_awgn_campaign`, `ldpc_bler_sweep`) already use; the OSD tool predates none of it. The dominant grid cell (order-2, 5.23 dB, ~4e7 blocks) pays the full cost.

Statistical correctness is unaffected; this is throughput only.

## Fix sketch

Deterministic lookahead inside the protocol loop: draw the per-cell block stream sequentially (RNG stays a cheap serial stream, preserving the exact block sequence), decode blocks in parallel workers, commit outcomes in block-index order, terminate at the block carrying the K-th error, and drop speculative blocks past it from every counter. The evaluator contract changes from `FnMut` to a per-thread evaluator (factory or `Fn + Sync`); the campaign binary adapts.

## Success Criteria

- REQ-01: The protocol evaluates blocks on multiple threads while committing outcomes in block-index order; for the same campaign and seed, the sampled block stream, all counters, the stopping index, and the receipt payload are identical to the sequential design's.
- REQ-02: The stopping design is preserved structurally: completion exactly at the block carrying the K-th block error; speculative blocks beyond it contribute to no counter.
- REQ-03: A test compares parallel and sequential runs of a scripted evaluator and asserts identical results; existing resume/byte-identity and protocol tests pass unchanged.
- REQ-04: Thread count defaults to available parallelism, is settable via a CLI flag, and appears in the receipt's invocation argv provenance.
- REQ-05: Measured speedup on an order-2 probe cell on the 24-thread host is reported in the issue closure notes.
title: OSD campaign protocol evaluates blocks single-threaded, idling 23 of 24 host threads
